name: Butterfree

abilities.name: tinted-lens
abilities.effect: Doubles damage inflicted with not-very-effective moves.

genderDifference: Female has black (purple in Generation V) spots on her lower wings

kanto.flavorText: In battle, it flaps its wings at great speed to release highly toxic dust into the air.

original-johto.flavorText: It flits from flower to flower, collecting honey. It can even identify distant flowers in bloom.

hoenn.flavorText: It has a superior ability to search for delicious honey from flowers. It can seek, extract, and carry honey from flowers blooming over six miles away.

original-sinnoh.flavorText: It loves the honey of flowers and can locate flower patches that have even tiny amounts of pollen.

extended-sinnoh.flavorText: It loves the honey of flowers and can locate flower patches that have even tiny amounts of pollen.

updated-johto.flavorText: Water-repellent powder on its wings enables it to collect honey, even in the heaviest of rains.

original-unova.flavorText: It loves the honey of flowers and can locate flower patches that have even tiny amounts of pollen.

updated-unova.flavorText: It loves the honey of flowers and can locate flower patches that have even tiny amounts of pollen.

kalos.flavorText: The wings are protected by rain-repellent dust. As a result, this Pokémon can fly about even in rain.

updated-hoenn.flavorText: Butterfree has a superior ability to search for delicious honey from flowers. It can even search out, extract, and carry honey from flowers that are blooming over six miles from its nest.

original-alola.flavorText: When attacked by other Pokémon, it defends itself by scattering its poisonous scales and fluttering its wings.

updated-alola.flavorText: Nectar from pretty flowers is its favorite food. In fields of flowers, it has heated battles with Cutiefly for territory.

letsgo-kanto.flavorText: Its wings, covered with poisonous powder, repel water. This allows it to fly in the rain.

swsh.flavorText: It collects honey every day. It rubs honey onto the hairs on its legs to carry it back to its nest.
